Published online:
        Not specified in article
    Geographic focus:
        Europe — Germany (Leipzig), with links to Ukraine, France, Lithuania, Poland, UK

    Temporal focus:
        T1. Historical observation [YES] — References prior Leipzig firebomb (July 2024), Lithuanian trial, and Ukraine cargo operations since Feb 2022
        T2. Forward-looking immediate [YES] — Ongoing investigation, elevated threat posture, airport security review
        T3. Long-term development [YES] — Escalating hybrid warfare pattern targeting NATO/European logistics infrastructure

    Synopsis:
        A bomb-laden drone was discovered at Leipzig/Halle airport near Ukrainian military cargo aircraft, with investigators citing a faulty detonator as the only thing preventing a potentially catastrophic explosion. The airport — a key NATO, German military, and Ukrainian logistics hub — appears to have been deliberately targeted in what German officials describe as a "professional hybrid threat scenario" linked to foreign state actors, with Russia the primary suspect. A second drone reportedly struck a DHL cargo plane mid-approach. The incident marks a significant escalation in hybrid sabotage operations on European soil.

At this stage, the Leipzig incident targets military logistics, not gas assets — hence a low but non-zero implicit score.
